COMMITTING: git push is 403 'denied to Onyx-Node' for the fixer too, not only for subagents - the App has no write access to kavopdf/app over HTTPS git. It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

context: 041122 renders 10 pages against the source's 9 (it was 11 when this run started, 12 before that). THIS RUN FIXED THE FOLIO PAGE. On page 7 the page draws a rule above its folio and a frame round the sheet, so the ruled pass handed the folio '7' back as the table's LAST ROW - a real drawn cell (363/10636/456 tw, trHeight 827 tw) whose only text is the sheet number, sitting in the band between the content rule at y=800.4 and the foot frame. Written as a row it is charged its whole 41.4 pt band on a page whose content already ends at 800.4 of 842, so the renderer broke the sheet and the folio cost a page of its own. DocxWriter.table() now detects a trailing row that is only a folio with its baseline in the page's bottom band (>0.88 page height), keeps it out of the table's height, and emits it as an anchored line at its own x/y - the same treatment the flow path's folio rule gives. Measured: 11 pages -> 10, doc share5 97.62 -> 86.25, worst page 7 -> 9, text_recall unchanged. NO-REGRESSION PROOF, and it is stronger than a gate run: all 213 documents were re-converted with the patched engine and compared entry by entry inside the .docx; 212 of 213 are byte-identical in every zip entry, so their renders and their scores cannot have moved. Only 041122 differs. benchmarks/RANKING.csv was therefore NOT rewritten - a full 213-document position sweep is hours of instrument time in one slot, and editing one row of the published table by hand is exactly the workaround this pipeline forbids; the next run's gate will pick the new number up when it measures. STILL OPEN, and it is the last extra page: the instruction page (our p8) stops at y=683.6 with 158 pt of sheet unused and spills 17 lines to p9. Mechanism measured, not guessed: w:cantSplit is written on EVERY row and it is a promise the engine cannot keep - strip all 86 occurrences from the same .docx and the page takes 166 lines instead of 154 and the spill falls from 17 to 5, so cantSplit is 12 of the 17 and row height the other 5. Not fixed because 26 of 213 documents carry a row written taller than 60 pt and none of them could be measured this run.
